pill.desc: clear to slightly opalescent, colorless to slightly yellow solution in a single-dose vial

tell: A PD-1 blocking antibody with a 22-day terminal half-life, given as a 30-minute infusion every 3 or 6 weeks.

clues.text: Volume of distribution at steady state is only 6.0 L. Clearance falls about 23% from the first dose to steady state, to 195 mL/day, and accumulation is 2.1-fold.
A humanized immunoglobulin of about 149 kDa, produced in recombinant Chinese hamster ovary cells.
A BLA product: a 100 mg/4 mL single-dose vial, given as 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks.
No boxed warning and no contraindications. Fatigue, musculoskeletal pain and rash are among the most common adverse reactions.
Many cancers, starting with unresectable or metastatic melanoma, and including non-small cell lung cancer.
Binds the PD-1 receptor on T cells and blocks PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing inhibition of the anti-tumor immune response.
The generic name begins with P and has thirteen letters.
